podcast.title: Diverse Production Work
podcast.body: Richardson worked on records for a range of artists including Alice Cooper, Bob Seger, and what sounds like "the Almond Brothers in Russian." "He also worked on records for Alice Cooper and Bob Seeger and the Almond Brothers in Russian a ton of others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Life and Career
podcast.body: Jack Richardson, born in Toronto in 1929, initially pursued a career as a musician. In the 1950s, he worked for the CBC before transitioning to the advertising industry in 1960, where Coca-Cola was his largest client. "He was born in 1929 and he started as a musician, but then went to work for the CBC in the 1950s before bailing for the advertising industry in 1960."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Entry into Music Production
podcast.body: In the late 1960s, Richardson entered the music industry, becoming the producer for The Guess Who during their most successful period. "In the late 60s, he got into the music industry and was the guest who was producer during their glory years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Legendary Canadian Producer
podcast.body: Jack Richardson is recognized as a legendary Canadian producer who was responsible for producing "all the guess who's best records." He is also the father of Garth Richardson, who produced Rage Against The Machine's debut album. "Jack did all the guess who's best records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mentoring Bob Ezrin
podcast.body: Jack Richardson provided Bob Ezrin with his first significant opportunity in a recording studio. "The guy who gave Bob his first proper gig in a recording studio was Jack Richardson, another Toronto guy."

xref.body: In the 1960s, Bob Ezrin secured a job at a recording studio with Jack Richardson, the producer for The Guess Who. He furthered his education by taking a summer course in music production taught by the legendary producer Phil Ramone. "In the 1960s, Bob got a job working in a recording studio with Jack Richardson, the guest who's producer. He also took a summer course in music production taught by the legendary producer Phil and Ramone."

xref.title: Evolution to Nimbus School of Recording & Media
xref.body: The studio eventually faced challenges and evolved into the Nimbus School of Recording & Media. It is currently run by Garth Richardson, son of the renowned Canadian producer Jack Richardson, and co-owned by famous Canadian producer Bob Ezrin, known for his work on Pink Floyd's *The Wall* and numerous Kiss records. "Couldn't make it after a while, and eventually evolved into the nimbus school of recording in media, and is run by Garth Richardson, son of the famous Canadian producer Jack Richardson, and is co-owned by Bob Ezren, the famous Canadian producer of Pink Floyd's The Wall, and a ton of kiss records."

xref.title: Family Background
xref.body: Garth Richardson is the son of Jack Richardson, a prominent Canadian record producer, and grew up observing his father's work with various bands. "And then came his kid, Garth. Garth Richardson grew up watching his dad work with all these bands."

xref.title: Producer of Rage Against The Machine
xref.body: Garth Richardson is credited with producing Rage Against The Machine's debut record, contributing to its acclaimed audio quality. He is the son of Jack Richardson, a legendary Canadian producer known for his work on The Guess Who's most successful albums. "Props to Garth Richardson, the son of legendary Canadian producer Jack Richardson."
